LESSON: IDDAH

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Muamalat (Social Relations)
Topic 6.2: Iddah

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Iddah. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Explain the main ideas in Iddah
2. Practise Iddah at school and at home
3. Give Kenyan examples connected to Iddah

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. Explain the main ideas in Iddah
   In simple words: practise until you can explain the main ideas in Iddah. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. Practise Iddah at school and at home
   In simple words: practise until you can practise Iddah at school and at home. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

3. Give Kenyan examples connected to Iddah
   In simple words: practise until you can give Kenyan examples connected to Iddah. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Iddah using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Iddah in the examples.
2. Explain Iddah to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Iddah.
4. Practise one skill from this lesson with a friend.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Iddah using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Iddah important for a Grade 9 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Explain the main ideas in Iddah
2. Practise Iddah at school and at home
3. Give Kenyan examples connected to Iddah

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
